runtime_dispatch_drift.interpretation: The provider catalog labels all 54 actions INTEGRATED, but the live dispatcher only has concrete branches for 23. The other 31 fall through to ADAPTER_REQUIRED. The new source migration adds the missing handlers and must pass fresh replay before provider application.

idempotency_observations.interpretation: The live schema contains globally unique idempotency keys on member-owned records. The same caller-supplied key can collide across users or subjects. The reconciliation migration replaces these with owner/subject-scoped unique indexes while retaining global deduplication for system rows with null owner/actor where applicable. This is a schema/function finding, not proof of an observed exploit.

member_owned_scopes.remediation: partial UNIQUE(user_id,idempotency_key) for member orders; retain global unique key for null-user system orders
partial UNIQUE(user_id,idempotency_key) for member tasks; retain global unique key for null-user system tasks
partial UNIQUE(user_id,idempotency_key) for member events; retain global unique key for null-user system events; advisory lock prevents duplicate axis mutation
partial UNIQUE(actor_user_id,idempotency_key) for member events; retain global unique key for null-actor system events
partial UNIQUE(actor_user_id,idempotency_key) for member audit records; retain global unique key for null-actor system records

idempotency_observations.verification: Provider ledger and scoped indexes are confirmed. The live helper definitions do not yet contain the complete immutable payload-conflict guards. Apply the new follow-up migration only after fresh replay and security/adapter regression probes pass.

dispatcher.interpretation: The live function definition was inspected and matched all 53 canonical module_read action branches plus the dedicated consultancy intake write branch. This verifies SQL dispatcher branch coverage only; it does not establish that every HTTP route, user journey, external provider, or page is operational.
